The Uddhārakośa composed by Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, page 3) [1.5]
Once, on a mountain peak made of crystal and thickly covered with forests,
Pārvatī and Śambhu stood together, intent upon the protection of the world.
Pārvatī spoke these beneficial words to the Supreme Lord:
"O God of gods, best among deities, whose mind is characterized by compassion and the three qualities!"
O God, by whom was the Goddess Bhagavatī Mahātripurasundarī revealed in this manifest world of moving and unmoving beings, both auspicious and cruel? (3)
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, for out of curiosity I shall tell you that which is to be kept secret.
On the most meritorious bank of the Revā, there is a virtuous city named Śrīgarbhā.
There is [a city] renowned throughout the three worlds, the crest-jewel of the entire surface of the earth.
In that place was a holy site of ascetic groves, frequented by the best of Brahmins, gods, and Gandharvas, and filled with various kinds of trees.
[1.14] In that meritorious penance grove, though frequented by the lords of sages,
there was a seer named Dakṣiṇāmūrti who was devoted to his worship.
Though he was a boat for the ocean of various scriptures, he became a treasury of all the Āgamas.
Once, he came to the Revā river, which was endowed with meritorious waters, in order to bathe.
Pleased with his previous meritorious deeds,
Mahātripurasundarī, the protectress, remained stationed in the midst of the water for him.
Instructed by the Goddess, that crest-jewel of the lords of sages [attained] his own root-mantra, which is pure, of the nature of nectar, swiftly bestowing fruit, and to be kept secret.
From that time forward, meditating upon that mantra and reciting the hymn within his heart,
O Great Goddess, he desired by its power to compose this book.
Merely by his grace, that sage, who was honored by the lords of sages,
composed the work known as the *Uddhārakośa*, an ocean of mantras.

O Goddess worshipped by the three worlds, having examined various other texts, from that time forth, O Queen of Gods, the work known as the *Uddhārakośa*, which is determined according to all the Āgamas, became famous upon the circle of the earth. (12)
The Goddess said:
O God of gods, Lord of the universe, bestower of grace upon devotees!
I wish to hear the [treatise] known as the Uddhārakośa, as determined by various Āgamas.
O Dhūrjaṭi, out of supreme affection, I desire to speak; you should deign to do so.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Pārvatī, for I shall explain the extraction of the mantras beginning with Tripura—
the unsurpassed extraction of the mantras of the ten Vidyās of the Goddesses.
[1.19] Listen as I speak of that work called the *Uddhārakośa*, which is definitively established by all the Āgamas, revered above all other texts, and the foremost of all compositions. (p. 5) 15.
By his mere grace, Dakṣiṇāmūrti spoke to his disciple named Akṣobhya concerning all the collections of extractions (uddhāra).
Listen, O highly fortunate student, endowed with devotion to the Goddess, to this secret which is difficult even for all the worlds and the gods to attain. (17)
O Goddess, at that moment, the Lord of Sages, Dakṣiṇāmūrti, spoke this supreme work to his disciple, who was pleasant of speech.
O Maheśvarī, listen as I speak of that which was spoken by Him in the past; hear of the power it possesses for the gods and the deities. (19)

And it is said in the Vāmakeśvara:
"One should join the Praṇava, Parā, Lakṣmī, Vīci, and Veśyā;
then the Moon, Maṭha, and thereafter Grahādhipataye. (17)
Then for Bṛhaspati, then Jīmūtabījaka, Padma, Lakṣmī, Nīraja, Vāsanā, and likewise Paṅkaja; at the end, Nīra is declared—this is the twenty-five-syllable mantra. (18)
Auspiciously: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ bkhrīṃ aiṃ glauṃ,
to Bṛhaspati, the lord of the planets.
Vīṃ ṭhaḥ śrīṃ ṭhaḥ aiṃ ṭhaḥ svāhā.
Now, regarding Candra, it is said in the Kālīpaṭala (p.
The three-eyed one (tryakṣa), the deer-eyed one (hariṇākṣī), and Kuntī, joined with the seed-syllable;

having added the word "hare," conjoined with the void (śūnya) and the anusvāra—then the seed of dance (nāṭyabīja) is in the middle, and at the end of the moon (candrāya) it is known as Aśmarī. || 19 ||

(40) Now, the extraction of the seed-syllable of the dance (*nāṭyabīja*): And it is said in the *Bhairava-tantra*: "The seed-syllable of the dance is *naṭana*; *tāṇḍava* is the seed-syllable of the rhythmic dance (*nṛtta*)."
And the four seeds, both natural and artificial. || 20 ||
Aloud: Oṃ śrīṃ krīṃ hrāṃ caṃ, salutation to the Moon.
These indeed are proclaimed as the five types of grahas of the five arrows. || 21 ||
Now follows the extraction of the mantras for the three planets.
First, regarding Mars,
it is stated in the *Śāradā-ṭīkā*:

The seed-syllable of Hariṇī, Rukmiṇī, the Lord of the Night (Śarvarīpati), the Piercer (Vedha), and then the seed-syllable; thereafter "to the Lord of Planets" (grahādhipataye), and at the end "to Bhauma" (bhaumāya); milk (payaḥ) is declared at the conclusion—this is the fifteen-syllable mantra. || 22 ||
(41) Now, regarding piercing (*vedha*), the extraction of the seed-syllable (*bījoddhāra*):
Piercing is the seed, the method, Brahmā, and the self-born seed itself;
there are four seed-syllables, both artificial and otherwise. (23)
[4.23] *Prakāśa*: Aiṃ Hmauḥ Śrīṃ Drāṃ Kaṃ.
Svāhā to Bhauma, the lord of the planets!
Now, regarding Saturn (Śanaiścara),
it is stated in the Āgama-laharī: "The seed-mantra is remembered as the syllable *tāra* (om), followed by *lajjā* (hrīṃ) and *śrī* (śrīṃ), and the three-headed one (*tri-śiraḥ*)."
Then, indeed, [one should offer] to Śanaiścara, the universal monarch among the planets. || 24 ||
Madana, Vāsanā, Śakti, and finally Nīra are proclaimed; O Goddess of Gods, this twenty-syllable mantra is remembered as belonging to Śanaiścara. || 25 ||
Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, to the emperor of the planets, Śanaiścara.
klīṃ aiṃ saḥ svāhā ||
Now, for this very Rāhu:
the Praṇava is the tongue, the pair of yugas is the two banks, and the thunder is the roar.
Then the fire-god [spoke] to Ṭaṅkadhārin and Rāhu. || 26 ||
[4.30] Lajjā, Lakṣmī, and Bhīmā are likewise mentioned at the end; the forest is proclaimed [therein].
Just as the twenty-syllable *bāla* mantra of Rāhu bestows desired fruits, so too [is this].
(42) Now, the extraction of the seed-syllable of *garjita* is stated in the *Svatantra*:
"Garjita, the seed-syllable of sound, as well as stanita and rasita."
And there are four seed-syllables (bījas), both artificial and others. || 28 ||
Aloud: Oṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ ṭaṃ, to Ṭaṅkadhārin Rāhu.
raṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ bhaiṃ svāhā ||
Following this, in verses 24 and 25, there is a repetition of the mantra,
and the deities of Śambhu’s three eyes have been described by me: "O Śivā, on an auspicious day, the practitioner should accomplish the mantras of the planets."
Now, regarding Ketu, it is stated in the *Tantrāmuktāvalī*:
"The syllable *praṇava* (Oṃ), followed by *sakalā vṛṣṭiḥ*, and then *krūrarūpiṇe*."
After that, Ketu, Śaṅkhapāda, Payas, and likewise Candra;
O Goddess, this is the great fifteen-syllable mantra of Ketu.
[4.33] (43) Now, the extraction of the seed of rain:
the seed of rain is the hailstone (*karaka*), while the rain-stone (*varṣopala*) is that which falls during the rainy season.
And there are four other artificial seed-syllables (bījas), beginning with *krūṃ*. || 31 ||
Thus, in the Muṇḍamālā Tantra.
Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ krūṃ,
to the comet of cruel form!
Aiṃ Sauḥ Svāhā.
The mantras of these nine planets have been spoken by me;
today, O Goddess of Gods, I shall indeed declare the mantras for the castes to you.
For the benefit of the world, keep this treasury more secret than the most secret;
by the mere knowledge of which, a practitioner becomes a master of mantras. (33)

Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Treasury for Extracting the Mantras of the Nine Planets," in the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Āgamas, composed by the venerable Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 4 ||
[5.7] The sages said:
O Brahmarṣi, you are a son of Brahmā and one who has reached the further shore of the ocean of the Āgamas.
O illustrious Lord, you are gracious toward us out of compassion. (1)
Indeed, various scriptures have been heard by us from the lotus of your mouth;
now we truly wish to hear the treasuries of mantras for the castes.
Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
"Listen, all you sages, to me as I duly [expound] the treasury of mantras of the letters, which issued forth from the mouth of Tripura. (3)
Īśvara said: Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the very extensive treasury of mantras,
which was previously indicated to the sages by Dakṣiṇāmūrti.
And it is said in the *Tripurātilaka*:
"The seed-syllable of the Self (*ātma-bīja*) is the letter *A*; the end of the self (*svānta*) is indeed the seed-syllable of the Heart (*hṛd-bīja*);
and the mind (*mānasa*) is the seed-syllable of the Mind (*manas-bīja*), which is remembered as belonging to the Grandfather (*paitāmaha*)."
O Goddess of the Suras, another falsehood is to be known as [the meaning] of the letter *a*. || 5 || *a* ||
It is said that "void," "space," "sky," "ether," and "of Viṣṇu" [are synonyms];
however, another [form], "ākāra," is declared to be false in the Bhairava-tantra. (6) || Ā ||
Likewise, Indrabīja, Jiṣṇu, Marutvān, Maghavā, and Hari;
one should state that the letter *i* belongs to Śiva, while the other is artificial.
O Mistress of the Gods, this has been declared by me in the Bhairava Tantra. || 7 || || i ||
p.
60) Likewise, *buddhi* is the seed of *medhā*, and *mati* is the seed of *dhī*;
similarly, the *aindra* [mantra] should be known as the supreme truth of the vowel *ī*.
O Goddess of the Suras, O Śivā, this was spoken by me in the Tripurātilaka. || 8 || || ī ||
The two *aindra* seeds are *i* and *ī*.

The seed-syllable *rut*, likewise *nandā*, *vāmana*, the seed-syllable *vānta*, *saurya*, and the seed-syllables beginning with *u*— these and other artificial ones have been declared by me in the *Sarvasva* of Kubjikā, O Sovereign of the Gods. (9) || u ||

O Goddess of the gods, *kaca-bīja*, as well as *keśa*, *śiroruha*, and *mūrdhaja*—these are synonyms for hair; O Supreme Goddess, I have declared that *aindava* and *anṛta* are other names for the letter *ū* in the *Śiromaṇi* of Sundarī. *Ū*.

"Pāpmā-bīja, as well as pāpa, kilbiṣa, and likewise kalmaṣa; likewise kiṃkarī-bīja, and the supreme Māṅgala-anṛta—O Śivā, these have been declared by me in this secret doctrine of the syllable Ṛ belonging to Kālī. || 11 || || Ṛ ||

The seed-syllable of grace (*kṛpā*), the seed-syllable of compassion (*dayā*), and likewise the farmer (*karuṇā*) [are derived from] the letter *ṛ*; the falsehood of the letter *ṛ* is otherwise spoken in the Viśvayāmala. 12. Ṛ.
The two universal seeds should be known as the syllable *ḷ* and *namaḥ*.
O Śivā, I have declared that *gaurvaṃ* is the manifest seed and the seed of the universe.
The other [seed], *anṛtam*, belongs to the syllable *ḷ*; this has been stated in the Rudrayāmala. || 13 || *ḷ* ||
The seed-syllable of Gaṅgā, the celestial river, the heavenly pond, and the river of heaven;
Śaukra, the other, and the unreal—these, O Goddess, have been remembered by me as the [meanings] of the letter *ḷ* in my own composed work, the *Mantrasāgara-tantra*. || 14 || *Ḷ* ||
(61) The eleventh [vowel] is the *mātṛkā*, and likewise the *latābīja*;
the *allībīja* and the *vārākī*—one may speak of these as other than untruth. (15)

Furthermore, O Sovereign of the Gods, I have explained the significance of the letter *e* in the work titled *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*, which was composed by the most excellent of mantra-experts. || 16 || || e ||
Vāgbhava, the upper seed-syllable (ūrdhvabīja), Cāraṇa, Caṇḍikeśvara, Candra, Carmavasana, and likewise Vāsanā. || 17 ||
O Goddess, although she possesses beautiful limbs, she is also skinless; furthermore, her measure is twelvefold.
This supreme falsehood regarding the vowel *ai* has been declared by me, O Goddess, in the *Tripurāsarvasva* treatise composed by Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 18 || || *Ai* ||

The *praṇava*, likewise the *tāra*, the three-eyed one (*tryakṣa*), and *tomā* as well as *tryambaka*; *trāsa*, *tārava*, O Goddess of Gods, and *kaitava*—these were remembered by me even when the *Chinnāśiromaṇi* was composed by me myself. || 19 || || o ||
Thus, the seed of liberation, liberation itself, knowledge, and the seed of nirvāṇa—along with the Āgastya [mantra]—have been declared by me in this Bhairava Tantra. || 20 || || au ||

The seed-syllable *Aṃ*, the seed of the tree, the footed plant, that which grows from the earth, and the tree-born—these have been declared by me; anyone who would speak otherwise has spoken untruth. Thus it is stated in the *Siddhasārasvata* treatise, revealed by Brahmā himself. (21) || Aṃ ||

O Goddess, I have declared to you the *nāgabīja*, the *bhūdhara*, the *bhāgyabīja*, and the *bhāvana*; the syllable *aḥ* is known as the eternal (*dhruva*) and supreme truth, [taught] in this *Tripurasundarīsarvasva* treatise which is difficult for all to attain. || 22 || *Aḥ*.
[5.30] The letter *ka* is the seed-syllable of the head, and the seed-syllable of the crown is that of Varuṇa;
it is the seed-syllable of Brahmā, the Ordainer, the Self-born, and indeed the seed-syllable of Svayambhū.
I have explained the letter *ka*; one should speak of another falsehood [regarding it] in this *Chinnārahasya* treatise, O daughter of Parvateśvara. *Ka*.
The seed-syllable *namaḥ*, the *puṣkara*, the sky-seed (*dyaubīja*), the *cakravāluka*,
and the seed-syllable of Vaiṣṭaraśrava were proclaimed by Tripurā herself in the *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*, which is difficult to obtain even for me. || 25 || || Kha ||
Śivabīja, Śambhu, Śarva, and Śaṅkara—these are the meanings of the letter *ga*. Any other [meaning] spoken by me, O beloved, is false.
This is found in the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi* treatise, which is difficult to obtain even in heaven. *Ga*.
The seed-syllable of the Jina, the possessor of the six superknowledges, and likewise the seed-syllable of the Conqueror of Māra;
Māyātmaja, Arkabandhu, Gautama, and Anṛta—the supreme—these are declared by me as the syllable *gha* in the Rudrayāmala treatise. *Gha*.
The six-faced one, born of the arrow, Skanda, is the seed-syllable of Kumāra;
Śāmbhava is the seed-syllable of Śāligī, while another is remembered as Anṛta.
This has been declared by me in the *Kubjikāsarvasva*, O you who are worshipped by the three worlds. (28) || Ṅa ||
The seed of drama (*nāṭyabīja*) is *naṭana*, and the seed of dance (*nṛttabīja*) is *tāṇḍava*; this has been declared by me for the letter *ca* in the *Bhairavatantra*. (29) || *ca* ||
The seed-syllable of Śani, that of Arkaja, likewise the seed-syllable of Paṅgu, Kāla, the seed-syllable of Saura, Sūti, and the seed-syllable of Sundara.
And the seed-syllable *chaṃ* has been proclaimed by me in the Vāmakeśvara scripture, O Śivā. || 30 || || cha ||
The two seed-syllables of Śani are *cha* and *ja*.

The seed-syllable *sta* refers to the breast, as well as the "produced from the chest" (*uroja*) and the "born from the heart" (*hṛjja*). This has been declared by me regarding the letter *ja*; anything else would be false.
Even in the treatise on the ornaments of the scriptures composed by Bhairava, [this is so]. || 31 || || *Ja* ||

The seed-syllable of desire is *spṛhā*, longing, and the seed-syllable of greed is the tetrad; this has been declared by me for the letter *jha*. O Goddess, in the *Vāmakeśvara* treatise, renowned throughout the three worlds, another [meaning] is recorded as being untrue. *Jha*.
The seed-syllable of Yama, the seed-syllable of Time, Kṛtānta, Samavartin, Kīnāśa, and the seed-syllable of Death— these are remembered by me as belonging to the letter *ña*,
O beloved, in the *Tripurāsarvasva* treatise, which is difficult to obtain in the three worlds. (33) || *ña* ||
The two seed-syllables of time are ñaṃ and chaṃ.

"Thundering," "the seed-syllable of sound," "rumbling," and likewise "resounding"—these are the meanings of the letter *ṭa* as declared by me in my own tantra, O goddess worshipped by the gods. (34) [Ṭa]"

Padma, paṅkaja, payoja, nīraja, and likewise ambuja—these five, O Goddess of Gods, are the artificial seed-syllables beginning with the letter *ṭha*, as well as others; they have been declared by me in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra. || 35 || ṬHA ||
Siṃhikā is the seed-syllable of Sarasī, and likewise the seed-syllable of Reṇukā;
the seed-syllable of Añjanī is well-known, while another is recorded as Anṛta.
O Goddess, the [seed-syllable] of the letter Ḍa has indeed been taught by me in the Rudrayāmala treatise. Ḍa.
[5.44] Vāyu, bīja, anila, samīraṇa, and likewise marut;
samīra, āśuga, vāta, and śvasana— the seed-syllable— should be known.
Regarding the letter *ḍha*, I have explained it; one should speak nothing else that is false. || 37 || ḌHA ||
The two seed-syllables of Vāyu are Ḍhaṃ and Yaṃ, according to the Bhairava Tantra.
The two seed-syllables of Āśuga are ṇaṃ and ḍhaṃ.
The seed-syllable of the arrow (vāṇa) is likewise the seeker (mārgaṇa), the feathered shaft (pattrin), and the swift one (āśuga);
according to another [reading] in the Bhairavatantra treatise, it is falsehood (anṛta) for the letter Ṇa. Ṇa.

*Rātri* is the seed-syllable of night, the seed-syllable of darkness (*tamas*), and indeed the seed-syllable of the *tāmasī* [nature]. *Kṣapā* and *kṣaṇadā* are other seeds; one should speak of them as such. In the text *Kubjikāsarvasva*, that seed-syllable has been remembered by me. (39) || ta ||
The seed-syllable *vi*, the cavity, the hollow, and the world of the Nāgas—these I have declared as the letter *tha* in the *Kulikārṇava-tantra*. (40) [Tha]
The seed-syllable *cakri* is known as the seed of the serpent; it refers to the snake, the *kākodara*, and the *uraga*.
It is remembered as the seed of the coiled one (*bhogin*), the *bhujaṅga*, and the *bhujaṅgama*. (41)
The letter *da* has been explained by me; another [letter] is traditionally held to be false.
This was composed by Dakṣiṇāmūrti in the *Svatantra*, O Goddess of the God of Gods. (42) || *da* ||

The letter *dha* is known as the flower-seed (*puṣpabīja*), the blossom (*prasūna*), procreation (*prasūti*), and likewise good offspring (*suprajā*); its opposite is falsehood (*anṛta*). It is remembered as the tilaka of Tripurā. (43) [Dha]
Alkaline seed, salt, rock salt, the boar, the wolf, the wild boar, and falsehood— these others have been declared by me, O Goddess of the Gods,
in the world-renowned treatise on Tripurā, the *Śiromaṇi*. || 44 || || na ||
[5.52] Fish, the seed of fish, and likewise the seed of the sapharī;
the seed of the jhaṣa— this I have declared in the *Chinnāśiromaṇi* treatise.
O Śivā, when the paths of the tortoise and the fish are traversed, the seed-syllable is similar [to both].
There is no mutual difference between the letter *pha* and the letter *pa*; however, regarding pronunciation, extraction, and writing, their natural forms are distinct. (46) [Pa]

O beautiful lady, in the *Śāradā-paṭala* chapter of the scripture renowned throughout the three worlds, O auspicious one, I have declared that *kūrma*, *bīja*, *kamaṭha*, *karkaṭa*, and *kulīraka* are synonyms for *kacchapa* (tortoise), while any other [term] is false. || 47 || || Pha ||

A wave (*ūrmi*), a ripple (*vīci*), and likewise a surge (*taraṅga*)—this triad is traditionally taught. O Sovereign of the Gods, it should be known that the other [aspects] are unreal, as declared by me in the *Kālikāsarvasva* treatise revealed by Brahmā himself. (48) || ba ||
"Bhadrikā, Bhāsvatī, and Bhīmā—these are the supreme [forms] of the letter Bha, which is untruth.
This has been declared by me in the *Muṇḍamālā-tantra*, O Sovereign of the Gods. (49) || BHA ||
The seed of the *dulī*, the seed of the *śilī*, the frog (*maṇḍūka*), the *durdura*, and the seed of the female frog (*bhekī*) have been declared by me; another is remembered as being false.
Thus, O daughter of Parvateśvara, it is stated in the *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*. 50. || Ma ||

The seed-syllable of Vāyu, likewise the eloquent one (vāgmin), the seed-syllable of the Vaiśya, the syllable Śārṇa of Vīra, and the Vāpī—these have been declared by me in the Svatantra. || 51 || Ya ||
Agni, Repha, Vahni, Hutabhuj, and Havyavāhana—O Goddess of the Gods, these are the names for the letter *ra* taught by me in the Śyāmātantra. || 52 || *Ra* ||
[5.59] Darkness as a seed, as well as gloom, delusion, and even blindness—
these are declared by me to be the meaning of the letter *la* in the independent tantra composed by the Sage. *la*.
The seed-syllable of the cloud (*abhrabīja*) is *jīmūta*, meaning "water-bearer" or "that which is leaped over";
this has been declared by me for the letter *va* in the *Vāmakeśvara Tantra*.
The seed-syllable of the earth (*bhūbīja*), the seed-syllable of the ground (*dharaṇībīja*), is the letter *va*; thus it has been spoken by me. *Va*.
"Auspiciousness (kalyāṇa), well-being (śarma), peace (śam), and the auspicious (śubha)—this tetrad of the letter Śa has been declared by me in the Bhairava Tantra. (55) || Śa ||

The seed-syllable *śampā*, the seed-syllable of lightning (*taḍit*), the one whose delight is the flash of the hundredfold lightning, and likewise the seed-syllable *hrādinī*—this other [seed-syllable] is known as *asatya*.
O Queen of the Gods, I have declared this in the *Rudrayāmala* treatise. (56) || Ṣa ||
"Śakti," "shelter," and likewise "autumn" and "doubt" are to be known as the meanings of the letter *sa*; this has been declared by me in the work *Chinnāśiromaṇi*. (57) *Sa*."

The seed of the skin, the seed of luster, as well as beauty and supreme splendor, and space— these are remembered by me as the meanings of the letter *ha*, which is always honored by practitioners of mantra in the *Siddhasārasvata* treatise. (58) || *ha* ||

O beloved, in the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi*, I have declared that the seed-syllable of the gods (*devabīja*) is *nirjara*, *tridisa*, and *tridiveśaka*; the seed-syllable of the Suras is *gīrvāṇa*, *lekha*, and *amarabījaka*. This pertains to the letter *kṣa*. || 59 || *kṣa* ||
[5.60] O Goddess of the gods, O Śivā, I have proclaimed this treasury of phonemes (varṇa),
which is endowed with various mantras, O Goddess, and is determined according to all the Āgamas.

Thus ends the fifth ritual manual (kalpa), titled "The Exposition of the Treasury of All Phonemes," within the *Sarvāgamamantrasāra*, composed by the venerable Dakṣiṇāmūrti, known as the *Uddhārakośa*. 5.
[6.5] O Sovereign of the Gods, the individual names for the two-syllable [mantras] are *krīṃ*, *prīṃ*, *śrīṃ*, and *hmauḥ*;
this is the certain conclusion of all the Āgamas.
Today, O Goddess, I shall declare to you the three deities of the worlds,
which were formerly spoken by Dakṣiṇāmūrti himself to the sages.
Bhavānī, O Goddess of the lords of gods, is the second Bagalāmukhī;
Indrākṣī is the third; these three are the deities of the three worlds.
I shall declare their mantras to you; listen, O Pārvatī.
These must not be told to just anyone; they must not be told, O fair-faced one.
First, the extraction of the Bhavānī-mantra is stated in the Muṇḍamālā-tantra:
"The Praṇava, two lotuses, a pair of three-eyed ones, and again Parā."
The two deer-eyed ones (hrīṃ), the beard (haḥ), Hara (haḥ), joined with two ṭhas (ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ). || 5 ||
Aloud: Oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
p. 69) [6.9] Now, regarding Bagalāmukhī, it is said in the Āgamalaharī:
The seed-syllable of the tree is declared to consist of two syllables;
this mantra should be known as having two heads. From that, one should extract the sprout.
O Blessed One, O Bagalāmukhī Devī, furthermore,
likewise [bind] the speech, the mouth, and the feet of all the wicked.
"Paralyze the tongue, likewise; pin the intellect, likewise twice;
destroy it twice, and likewise the seed-syllable of earth (MṚT). At the end, 'tryakṣa' (the three-eyed one) followed by 'payas' (water) is to be known; this is the mantra of fifty-two syllables. (8)
(44) Now, the extraction of the seed-syllable *mṛd* is stated in the *Bhairavatantra*: "The seed-syllable *mṛd*, the seed-syllable *mṛttikā*, the seed-syllable *mṛtsnā*, and *praśastikā*."
O daughter of Parvateśvara, falsehood is to be known as the ultimate softness.
Aloud: Oṃ hrīṃ, O Blessed One, Bagalāmukhī, Goddess, paralyze, paralyze the speech, the mouth, and the steps of all the wicked!
Pierce the tongue, pierce it! Destroy the intellect, destroy it!
Hlīṃ Oṃ Svāhā!
p. 70) [6.14] Now, regarding Indrākṣī, it is stated in the Rudrayāmala:
O Goddess, [the mantra consists of] the three-eyed one (tryakṣa), the two kuntīs, likewise the pair of kūrca-s,
the seed-syllable of prastha, the supreme Padmā, carmāṇa, and then the name.

Indrākṣī, Vajrahastā, at the end Lakṣmī and Lajjā, Puṣkara, the pair of banks (tīra), two Rasanas, Trāsa, Candra, Hara, and Vana; this is the twenty-eight-syllable mantra of Indrākṣī, the Goddess of the Gods. || 11 ||
(45) Now, the extraction of the seed-syllables of the *prastha*:
it is stated in the *Śāradāpaṭala*— the seed-syllable of the *prastha*, the seed-syllable of the *sānu*, as well as the *śikhara* and the *puṣkara*.
This is indeed the extraction of the seed-syllable *mlauṃ*; one should not speak anything else that is untrue.
Aloud: Oṃ krīṃ krīṃ hūṃ hūṃ mlauṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ Indrākṣi, O you who hold the thunderbolt in your hand!
Śrīṃ hrīṃ mlauṃ hūṃ hūṃ krīṃ krīṃ oṃ aiṃ phaṭ svāhā.
"O Goddess, these three deities of the world have been described by me; they were revealed in this worldly existence through devotion by Dakṣiṇāmūrti. (13)
[Now, concerning the Khecarīs:
Then, O Goddess of the lords of gods, I shall indeed declare the mantra of the Khecarī.
Relying upon which, the yogi may attain the portion that bestows the perfection of Khecarī.
And it is said in the Viśvayāmala:
"One should extract the tenth letter from Gīrvāṇa in reverse order;
then one should place the seed-syllable of Tamas, and after that, the seed-syllable of Māyā. (15)
Then one should give the seed-syllable of Śarad; this is proclaimed as the "Kūṭa.
The mantra should be known as the "head of the fourth" (the letter *au*); then the yogi should give the name, and then to Khecarī, at the end, the syllable *sauṣmaka* (*ha*) itself.
Prakāśam mala hrīṃ sauḥ, salutation to Khecarī.
Now, O Goddess of gods, I shall describe the meditations determined by the Āgamas for these deities and planets, O you who are worshipped by the gods. (17)
Likewise, the meditation of the seven Kumāras is determined therein;
likewise, O Pārvatī, hear from me in truth about those who are free from differentiation. 18.
Thus ends the sixth ritual manual (kalpa), titled "The Narration of the Treasury of the Three Goddesses Khecarīs," in the *Uddhārakośa* composed by the venerable Dakṣiṇāmūrti. || 6 ||
[7.9] Now, O Sovereign of the Gods, I shall first describe the meditation on the ten vidyās of Tripurā as taught in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra; listen to me.
Her body was adorned with divine garments, her eyes were like the sun, fire, and moon,
she wore the moon as a crown, and her luster was like that of snow.
I worship Tripura, who sits upon a lion-throne, who holds an axe and a sword in her two arms, and who is bowed to by Brahmā, Indra, and Viṣṇu. || 3 ||
Now I shall describe the meditation on Śrī as taught in the Rudrayāmala,
which is highly honored by sages, practitioners, gods, and groups of brahmins.
Lakṣmī, seated upon a lotus throne, with the sun and moon for her eyes, possessing the luster of rising gold, and holding a lotus, a conch, and a sword in her hands. (5)
I bow with devotion to her whose limbs are adorned with fragments of various pearls and gems, who has two arms, and who eternally bestows the fruits of the three worlds. 6.
Now, O Śivā, I shall describe the meditation on Vāgdevī, which bestows knowledge,
in this work titled Tantramuktāvalī, which is difficult to find even in heaven.
She whose face is as radiant as the full moon, who possesses the luster of camphor and the kunda flower,
and whose head is marked by the crescent moon— she who respectfully holds [these attributes] with her own hands.
I worship her who is mounted upon a lion, holding a lute, a rosary, a jar filled with nectar, and the science of knowledge; her body is adorned with divine ornaments and her breasts are lofty. 9.
[7.19] Now I shall explain the meditation on Tārā according to the Bhairava Tantra—
the Goddess who is devoid of differentiation and worshipped by sages and practitioners.
The goddess was adorned with serpents, possessing the cool luster of the moon and the radiance of a conch shell;
her neck and arms were encircled by bracelets of pearls and gems, and she wore red garments. || 11 ||

I worship Tārā, who holds a trident, lotus, sword, and mace; who is praised by the hosts of gods led by Vaikuṇṭha; who is eternally devoted solely to the protection of the three worlds; and who possesses three eyes. 12.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Bhuvaneśvarī; listen to that, which has been extracted from the Rudrayāmala, a text that bestows the desires of practitioners. (13)
With a face resembling a thousand rising suns, possessing full breasts and seated upon a lotus,
she respectfully holds in her arms a goad, a noose, a book, and a banner of victory.

I worship the three-eyed Mistress of the World within the lotus of my heart—she who is eternally praised with salutations, hymns, and other praises by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Indra, and the sages. || 15 ||
Now, O daughter of the mountain, I shall describe the meditation on Mātaṅgī, as found in my own work *Kubjikāsarvasva*, which is extremely difficult to obtain. (16)
She has a crest adorned with the crescent moon, possesses three eyes, and has the radiance of ten million moons and suns;
her girdle is bound with thousands of various jewels, and she is seated upon a corpse-throne.
I always meditate in my heart upon the enchanting Goddess Mātaṅginī, who joyfully bears a conch, a tomara-weapon, a paṭṭisa-spear, and a pair of lotuses in her arms. 18.
Now, O Maheśānī, I shall describe the supreme meditation on Śārikā, which has been extracted from the *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī* and is difficult for people to obtain. (19) [7.28] p. 74)
Her hands bear the auspicious conch, discus, mace, and a pair of lotuses;
her neck is adorned with a garland marked by the coils of the lord of serpents serving as a necklace and bracelets.
I meditate in my heart upon the illustrious Śārikā, who has three eyes and possesses the brilliance of a thousand rays of vermilion and saffron. 21.
Now, O Goddess of gods, O daughter of Parvateśvara, I shall describe the unsurpassed meditation on the Queen as taught in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra.
She has eyes like the cool-rayed moon, the morning sun, and fire;
she is four-armed and seated upon a deer-skin.
I worship the Queen Maheśī, who bears a conch, a lotus, a trident, and a sword, and whose form is like that of the snowy mountain. 24.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Bhedā, which bestows the fruits of one's desires;
it has been composed by me personally in the Niḥsmṛta-āgamoddyota. (25)
Resembling the mass of radiance from the rays of the rising cool-rayed moon,
she sits upon a full-blown lotus, holding a lute, the lord of serpents, and a conch shell.
Holding a sword and an axe in her four adorable arms, her chest was adorned with pearl necklaces and various kinds of gems. (27)
I bow to Bhavānī in the form of Bheḍā, who carries a vessel of rum, whose face is radiant with laughter, and who bestows the desired objects upon her practitioners. || 28 ||
[7.36] Now, O Goddess of the Gods, I shall describe the unsurpassed meditation on Jvālāmukhī,
as composed by me in the work *Jvālāśiromaṇi*.
I meditate in my heart upon Jvālāmukhī, whose hair is encircled by flames, who bears a lotus, a conch, a sword, and a mace, and whose pair of feet is placed upon a lion throne. 30.
Now I shall declare the meditation on Bhadrakālī as it was remembered by me, from the Vāmakeśvara Tantra composed by myself. (31)

I am never satiated by her who holds the shaven head of the Creator of the universe upon the palm of her lotus-hand, who laughs while speaking to the entire multitude of people, and who is constantly devouring them all.

I meditate upon Bhadrakālī, who is dark-complexioned like Viṣṇu and Śiva, the crusher of enemy hosts, holding a sword in her praiseworthy arms; she is as white as fresh water and is seated in the midst of corpses.

I shall proclaim the fourth meditation, which is free from recollection, within this nectar of the scriptures, renowned throughout this world of moving and unmoving beings, and revealed by Brahmā himself. (34)
She is Śivā, possessing two arms, white as the moon, holding a noose and a lotus, with her head encircled by matted locks and adorned with crescent moons set with various jewels.
I worship the fourth goddess, whose eyes are the sun, moon, and fire, whose face is white, who is seated upon a corpse-throne, and who is saluted by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara. 36.
O Goddess, I shall first describe the visualization of Chinnamastā as it is traditionally remembered,
according to my own work, the *Śiromaṇi*, a treatise on Tripurā.
Her forehead-surface was encircled by the rays of the moon; she possessed the splendor of ten million rising suns;
she bore a mass of highly precious jewels bound with flames; and she blazed with the pride of Kandarpa.

I shall always meditate upon the Goddess Chinnamastā within the lotus of my heart—she who holds a trident, a goad, a noose, a flute, a mace, and a lotus, who grants the desires of her devotees, and whose head is severed. (39)
O daughter of Parvateśvara, I shall now describe the meditation on Dakṣiṇakālī as it is remembered in this work, the Kālīrahasya.

She has the bones of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva for her necklace and girdle, her lower lip is red with betel, and she resembles an autumn cloud; she holds a trident, a mace, a lotus, a sword, a noose, and a goad.
I meditate upon that goddess Dakṣiṇakālikā, the Blessed Lady, who holds a conch and a pair of snakes, possesses ten arms, is seated upon a corpse-throne, and is clad in red garments. 42.
Now, O daughter of the Mountain, I shall describe the meditation upon Śyāmā, as it was declared by me in the Śyāmā-tantra within the ocean of all the Āgamas. (43)
Her two lotus feet are worshipped by the three worlds;
she possesses a form resembling a dark rain-cloud and has three eyes.
I worship the dark-complexioned goddess who holds a trident, a sword, and a great conch in her own arms, and who is seated upon a corpse. 45.
Now, O Goddess, I shall declare the meditation on Kālarātri, which is beyond recollection, as it was composed by me in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra. (46)

[7.56] I meditate in my heart upon the Great Goddess Kālarātri, who holds a trident, a lotus, a noose, and a goad in her four hands; she is smoke-colored, possesses three eyes, sits upon a lion throne, and wears yellow garments. 47.
O Goddess adorned with various ornaments, I shall speak; listen! I shall describe the visualization of Śrī Vajrayoginī as it is remembered in the Kulikārṇava. (48)
I worship Vajrayoginī, the auspicious one who has the moon, fire, and sun as her eyes, who holds a noose and a goad, who possesses two arms, and who is seated upon a lion. (49)
Now, O Goddess, I shall describe the meditation on Vārāhī as determined in the Tantra,
which bestows all desired objects, O beloved, in the Kulacūḍāmaṇi.

I meditate upon the stainless Varāhī within the lotus of my heart— she who has the crescent moon as her crest-jewel, who is two-armed and holds a trident and a goad in her hands, whose face is dark-hued, and who casts glances formed of the sun, fire, and moon.
Now, O Goddess of the Gods, I shall describe the supreme meditation on Śāradā, even though it has already been composed by me myself in the chapter on Śāradā within this treatise. (52)

I meditate in my heart upon the blessed goddess Śāradā, who has six arms and three eyes, whose face is smiling, whose lotus-feet are praised by the sage Śāṇḍilya, who stands upon a mountain, and who holds a trident. (53)
Now, O Goddess of gods, I shall describe the supreme meditation upon Kāmeśvarī Tripurā within this most excellent secret of all tantras; listen to it. 54.

I meditate in my heart upon that Kāmeśvarī, who has three eyes and the splendor of a thousand suns; she is seated upon a lion-throne, possesses two arms holding a sword, wears yellow garments, and is served by Viṣṇu and Maheśa. 55.
Now, O daughter of Parvateśvara, I shall describe to you the meditation on Gaurī according to the Bhairava Tantra, as composed by me in this work. (56)
[7.65] Fair-limbed, holding a lotus, three-eyed, clad in white garments, and riding upon a lion;
with her crest illuminated by the moon, her face smiling, she carries a mace with her two arms.
I worship that Blessed Goddess Gaurī, who grants the desires of her devotees, whose two feet are worshipped by Viṣṇu, Indra, Brahmā, Śiva, and the gods, and who is the lotus born from the mind.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Annapūrṇā; listen, O Goddess, as it has been revealed by me in the Bhairava Tantra, which is free from [ordinary] memory. (59)

I meditate upon that Annapūrṇā in my heart—she who has the crescent moon as her crest-jewel, two arms, and three eyes; she who holds a trident and a rosary in her two hands, sits upon a deer-seat, and wears a serpent as a sacred thread.
O beloved, I shall describe the meditation on Kulavāgīśvarī; listen to me, for she is difficult to attain even for me in this *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*.
I worship Kulavāgīśvarī, who holds a trident and a sword in her two arms, whose face is red, who resembles fire, who possesses three eyes, and who is seated upon a lion throne. 62.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Gaṇeśa, O Mother, who is worshipped by the gods;
you are the nectar that fills the ocean of the Āgamas, and you are difficult to attain in this world. 63.

I worship the son of Śiva, who has two, four, and fourteen colors; who dwells on the earth, holds a mace and a lotus, and wears a sacred thread; who walks upon two lions, possesses three eyes, and has the face of an elephant. 64.
Now I shall describe the meditation of the Youth; listen, O Pārvatī, as it has been composed by me in the Niḥsmṛta, which illuminates the Āgamas, O Śivā. (65)

[7.75] In my heart, I remember the primordial Kumāra, the bestower of desired boons, who is white as the Himālaya mountain, two-armed, whose body is entwined by serpents, who sits upon a peacock-throne, and who is the beloved son of the Queen of the Nāgas. 66.
O Haihaya, out of curiosity for you, I shall describe this meditation which is certain to bestow whatever is desired upon men and is most formidable. (67)
He had a thousand arms and a circular halo, having conquered the lord of the lords of the tamīcaras;
his face was like the moon, and he held a thousand quivers.
I meditate in my heart upon Kārtavīryārjuna, the lord of the world, who always wears white garments and stands amidst the king of horses. 69.
Now, O Goddess of gods, I shall describe the meditation upon that god Mṛtyuñjaya as it is traditionally remembered in the work known as the Kubjāśiromaṇi. (70)
He bears the Lord of the Gods, whose hair is illuminated by the moon, carrying a vessel of nectar;
with his lotus-hand he holds the moon, which is as stainless as ten million moons, like a lotus of his smile.
I meditate upon that Paśupati, the conqueror of death, who is imperishable, whose eyes are the sun, fire, and moon, and who holds in his palms a noose, a rosary, a goad, and a lotus.
Now, O daughter of the mountain, I shall describe the meditation on Sugrīva in this work titled Kulacūḍāmaṇi, which is composed as an ocean of mantras. (73)
With devotion, he beheld the youthful Lord of Monkeys, sixteen years of age, radiant with the brilliance of fire,
holding in his arms trees, maces, bows, and multitudes of arrows.
I meditate in my heart upon the divine Lord Sugrīva, the son of the Sun, who joyfully worships the venerable Lord of the Raghus, who is the very embodiment of the gods. 75.
[7.84] Then, O Daughter of Parvateśvara, I shall declare to you the meditation on Hanumān as it is taught in the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi* treatise, which is free from forgetfulness.

I meditate in my heart upon Hanumān, the beloved friend of Rāma, the sole hero of the world, the king of monkeys who has offered his salutation; he who resembles the peak of Mount Sumeru, the inconceivable, primordial, and worshipful one. 77.
Now, O Pārvatī, I shall describe to you the meditation on Bhairava,
as it is taught in the Bhairava Tantra, which bestows desired fruits.

One should remember in one's heart that Bhairava, the bestower of desired fruits—he who holds a skull in his hand, has a serpent for a sacred thread, possesses a dark complexion, carries a staff, has three eyes, is inconceivable, primordial, and is devoted to drinking wine. (79)
Now I shall describe the meditation on the Sun as determined in the Tantra, according to the *Tripurāsarvasva* treatise composed by Dakṣiṇāmūrti. (80)

I worship the primordial god Mihira within the lotus of my heart— the manifest deity, pure and radiant, beautifying the region of the earth with a thousand rays, mounted upon seven horses, and holding a noble banner in his hand.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Saumya according to the Bhairava Tantra; it is true and bestows all desired objects, and is honored by gods and asuras alike. (82)

I meditate upon Budha in the lotus of my mind—he who is the son of Soma, seated upon a swan, two-armed, with a form like the conch and the moon, holding a noose in his hand, a treasury of compassion, his limbs adorned with ornaments. (83)
Now I shall explain the visualization of Śukra as determined in the Tantra, as revealed by Brahmā himself in the *Kubjikāsarvasva* treatise. (84)

[7.92] I shall meditate upon Śukra within the lotus of my heart— he who resembles molten gold, has two arms, is compassionate, wears yellow garments, holds a pair of lotuses and a trident, sits in the *krauñca* posture, whose lotus feet are served by the gods, and who grants victory. 85.
Now I shall describe, O Pārvatī, the meditation upon the Jīva according to its true nature as taught in the Bhairava Tantra; it bestows all goals upon men. (86)

I remember my Guru, who is composed of fire, who holds a spear and a trident in his hands, whose lotus feet are praised by the foremost of the lords of gods, who is a treasury of wisdom, who appeared as a fish, and who possesses two arms, within the lotus of my mind. (87)
Now I shall describe the meditation on Candra; listen, O dear goddess, for it has been taught in the *Āgamoddyota* as a river of various meditations. 88.

I meditate upon the moon, the lord of the planets, who possesses the luster of a conch shell, who is dear to the deer, whose form is worthy of praise as he rests upon the crown of the Lord (Śiva), and who holds a pair of lotuses in his hands within the lotus of my heart. 89.
Now I shall declare the visualization of Bhauma as determined in the Tantra;
listen with a one-pointed mind, O beloved, in this *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*. 90.

I remember in my heart the compassionate Bhauma, who resembles the molten Ganges, who is seated upon a lion-throne with a lotus and sword in his hands, and whose lotus feet are worshipped by gods and asuras. 91.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Śani, which bestows the desired fruit;
it is remembered as auspicious and has been extracted from the nectar of the Āgamas, O Maheśānī. (92)

[7.100] I meditate upon Śani in the lotus of my mind— having the luster of blue collyrium, the beloved son of Mihira (the Sun), the lord of the planets, holding a noose and a serpent in his hands, two-armed, and the bringer of fear to both gods and demons. 93.
Now I shall describe the meditation on Saiṃhikeya; listen to it, for in the Vāmakeśvara Tantra, it is said that even when forgotten, it yields fruit for men. (94)

I worship within my heart Rāhu, the lord of planets, whose form is both terrible and praiseworthy, resembling a cool-rayed moon, sapphire, or fire; who has two arms, is the supreme protector of the three worlds, and bestows all that is desired. (95)
Now I shall describe the visualization of Ketu as determined by the Āgamas,
as it appears in the work *Āgamoddyota* within the *Mantrasāgara*, which is free from error.

I worship in the lotus of my mind the Ketu who possesses a tail, who strikes fear into people, who resembles a dark rain-cloud, who is a peerless hero, who is clad in black garments, and who holds a spear and a trident in his hands. 97.
Now, O Goddess of gods, I shall describe the supreme meditation on Bhavānī, which has been extracted from the *Kulacūḍāmaṇi* treatise, O Sovereign of the World. (98)

I worship Bhavānī, who holds a lotus, a conch, a sword, a shield, arrows, her own bow, a trident, and a threatening gesture; she who bestows fear, stands upon the head of Mahiṣa, and resembles fresh dūrvā grass. 99.
Now I shall proclaim the meditation on Bagalāmukhī as it has been handed down,
from the *Āgamāmṛtamañjarī*, which is honored by gods and demons. (100)

I bow to the auspicious Goddess Śivā, seated upon a lion-throne, wearing a beautiful crown set with various jewels and clad in yellow garments that bestow good fortune; her eyes are like the rays of the sun, fire, and the moon.

I worship in my heart the Goddess Śrī Bagalāmukhī, who resembles the noble son of Gaṅgā (Bhīṣma), whose limbs are ever resplendent with precious gems, who grants the desires of her devotees, and bestows liberation. 102.
Now I shall speak; listen, O Indrākṣī, to the supreme meditation, which emerged from the memory of the Lord of the World, in the Rudrayāmala scripture. (103)
She holds a garland, a goad, and a pair of lotuses; she possesses a thousand eyes and is auspicious.
Seated upon the back of the intoxicated Airāvaṇa, moon-faced, she is intent on the protection of the three worlds.

With my arms, I worship in my heart the supreme Indrākṣī, the mother of all beings, whose form is compassion, who delights in singing with her hands, who resembles a blooming lotus, and who is praised by the gods beginning with Brahmā. (105)

Now, O Maheśānī, I shall describe the supreme meditation on Khecarī, by meditating upon which a yogi becomes liberated while living in the Kali age; this has been extracted from the scripture known as the Bhairava Tantra, worshipped by the thirty gods. 106.
Her two feet are worshipped by sages with wide-awake lotuses and water-lilies;
her hands and face are white and dark respectively, and her crest is radiant with the white moon.

[7.113] I meditate in my heart upon Khecarī, the mother of the world, the bestower of spiritual accomplishments (siddhi), who has the sun, moon, and fire as her eyes, and who holds the gestures of fearlessness and a book. 108.
O Goddess of the gods, this collection of mantras and meditations for these [deities] is remembered;
it must not be given to just anyone, for it is a treasury containing the extraction of the texts.
The sages said:
Blessed is he whose son you are, having mastered all the scriptures. May you be victorious; please command us to depart for our own homes.
The illustrious Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
"Go now, all you sages; forgive me out of compassion.
Having been addressed thus, the sages, longing for the mantra, departed for their own homes. (111)
Īśvara said:
Having seen those beautiful tantras by that Dakṣiṇāmūrti, he composed the work called Uddhārakośa; keep it as the most secret of secrets.
The Goddess said:
"O Lord of the Gods, I have been purchased by you with this book.
Having spoken thus, they both went to a magnificent grove on Mount Kailāsa.
Both of them—the goddess Ambikā and the moon-crested god—[spoke]. || 113 ||

Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Determination of the Meditations on the Treasury of the Sixteen Goddesses, the Seven Goddesses, the Seven Kumāras, the Nine Planets, and the Four Goddesses," in the *Uddhārakośa*, the essence of all Āgamas, composed by the venerable Dakṣiṇāmūrti. 7.
